target_customer: Founders, business owners and small teams who want to build mobile and web apps without writing all the code, and agencies and freelancers
problem: Building mobile apps needs scarce engineering skill. Draftbit began as a visual builder that produced real React Native code and now uses AI agents plus a visual editor and paid human experts.
business_model: SaaS subscriptions plus paid expert build and management services
product_category: Low-code and AI app builder (developer tools)

founders.name: Brian Luerssen
prior_employers: OkCupid Labs (created it and was general manager)
previous_startups: Quantitative Insights (co-founder, medical imaging, later acquired)
founders.background_notes: Per the YC company page. Education not taken from an opened source.

founders.name: Tim Grace
founders.background_notes: Named Co-Founder and COO of Draftbit in the title of a Tech in Chicago podcast episode (May 2019), page not opened. Other sources name Peter Piekarczyk as CTO, not opened, so not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: A browser based visual editor that generates and exports working React Native code is standard front end engineering with hard parts in code generation and mobile build pipelines.

defensibility.rationale: Users export code, so lock-in is weak, and many no-code and low-code builders exist.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Later AI app builders (RapidNative, FlutterFlow) compete directly per comparison sites. Draftbit stayed independent and now builds on Claude Code and OpenAI Codex.

market_need_then: Mobile app development was costly and skill limited, and React Native had spread in 2017 to 2018. The 2017 pre-seed from Network Ventures suggests early investor interest. No dated demand statistics were found.

identity.logo: Official logo files offered in a media kit

branding.community_and_virality: Site claims 200k+ builders and a 4.8 rating (self-reported).

brand_strength.rationale: Short, plain name with a media kit, but no mascot or community evidence found, and it competes with similar names like Drafted.

pivots.to: AI agent app builder using the customer's Claude or ChatGPT plan
pivots.why: Not stated by a source, inferred from current product copy only, date approximate

outcome_analysis: Draftbit raised a small pre-seed in 2017 and a $3.2M seed in 2019, and has stayed at about ten staff. It repositioned to an AI app builder that runs on customers' own Claude or ChatGPT plans and claims 200k builders. No later priced round, layoffs or sale were found.
notes: Both rounds come from aggregators only (Startup Intros and Seedtable for pre-seed, Seedtable, Bouncewatch and Crunchbase for seed) and no press release or Form D was found, so amounts and investors are unverified in detail. Lead conflicts: Seedtable lists YC as lead, Crunchbase lists Fuel Capital and Floodgate. Seedtable also shows a 1M round in April 2019 and totals of 1.4M to 4.9M, not recorded. A search summary said the company was formerly Orchard and that founding year is 2017 or 2018, unverified. The pivot to AI is inferred from the current site and its date is approximate. Competitors: no 2018 dated source found, comparison pages are from later years.
